html:
With crystal-clear beaches where you can see straight to the ocean floor, untouched landscapes, and a peaceful island atmosphere, Phu Quy Island has become a dream destination for many travelers. Join us as we explore the most popular attractions on Phu Quy Island – a hidden gem of Binh Thuan Province.

Phu Quy is gradually making its mark on the Binh Thuan tourism map. Blessed with pristine beaches, turquoise waters, and unspoiled natural scenery, the island offers a rare sense of tranquility that captivates visitors from the very first moment.

Princess Ban Tranh Temple

According to legend, Princess Ban Tranh was exiled to a deserted island after disobeying her father, the king. Accompanied by only a few servants and a small boat, she reclaimed the land, fished, cultivated crops, and established the first settlements on the island. She taught the local people how to farm and grow crops, laying the foundation for life on Phu Quy Island.

In gratitude for her great contributions, local residents built a temple in her honor. Every year on the 3rd day of the Lunar New Year, the Princess Ban Tranh Temple Festival takes place, attracting many visitors traveling to Binh Thuan during the holiday season. The temple is a national historical relic, reflecting the cultural fusion between Cham and Vietnamese traditions and the spiritual life of the island’s people.

Phu Quy Lighthouse

Located on Mount Cam at an elevation of 108 meters above sea level, Phu Quy Lighthouse is one of the largest lighthouses in Vietnam. At night, its powerful light guides fishing boats safely home. To reach the lighthouse, visitors must climb more than 120 stone steps, passing uniquely shaped rocks formed by years of exposure to wind and sea.

From the top, travelers can enjoy panoramic views of Phu Quy Island’s poetic landscape: calm blue seas, fishing boats drifting in the distance, Mount Cam reflected in the water, and surrounding islets such as Hon Tranh, Hon Trung, and Hon Dao acting as natural shields against ocean storms.

Trieu Duong Bay

Trieu Duong Bay is considered the most beautiful beach on Phu Quy Island, featuring a long stretch of fine white sand and crystal-clear water. Coconut palms, whispering casuarina trees, and nearby islets like Hon Tranh and Hoa Son create a breathtaking natural painting.

The best time to swim here is in the late afternoon, when the sun softens and the sea becomes especially inviting. Trieu Duong Bay is also famous for its romantic sunsets, when the sky and sea glow in warm hues. Visitors can even experience local island life by joining fishermen in casting nets, pulling in the catch, and enjoying freshly caught seafood.

During festivals and holidays, Trieu Duong Bay becomes a lively gathering place for locals, yet it still retains its peaceful charm thanks to the island’s mild climate and sustainable tourism development.

Linh Son Pagoda – Cao Cat Mountain

Linh Son Pagoda is not only a spiritual destination but also one of the best viewpoints on Phu Quy Island. Situated atop Cao Cat Mountain, the pagoda offers a 360-degree view of the entire island. To the east lies the mysterious tomb of Master Sai Nai, believed to bring wisdom to those who visit. To the west, visitors can spot Mount Cam Lighthouse and Princess Ban Tranh Temple.

The sound of waves blending with the pagoda bells, along with the gentle scent of incense, creates a deeply peaceful and sacred atmosphere. Many travelers stop here to pray for good fortune and family well-being.

Wind Power Hill

Constructed in 2010 in the northern part of the island, Phu Quy Wind Power Hill is Vietnam’s first hybrid wind–diesel power project. It supplies electricity 24/7 for local residents and has become a unique check-in spot for visitors.

Unlike other wind farms, Phu Quy’s turbines stand against a backdrop of blue sea and green grasslands, where herds of cows graze peacefully. The simple white turbines contrast beautifully with the deep blue sky, creating a calm and nostalgic scene perfect for photography or even a relaxed outdoor picnic.

Infinity Lake

Often called the “Little Bali of Vietnam,” Phu Quy Island is home to the stunning Infinity Lake, located near Bai Nho – Ganh Hang. This natural rock pool connects directly to the open sea, creating the illusion of endless water stretching into the horizon.

The lake’s beauty changes throughout the day—from serene sunrise moments to vibrant midday colors and romantic sunsets. Its untouched charm has quickly made it one of the most sought-after photo spots on the island.

Hon Tranh Islet

Just 600 meters from Phu Quy Port, Hon Tranh is the largest of the ten surrounding islets. With no permanent residents except for a naval observation station, the islet remains largely untouched. Calm, crystal-clear waters make it an ideal destination for snorkeling and coral viewing at Vung Phat Marine Conservation Area.

Hon Tranh’s volcanic rock formations, colorful coral reefs, and peaceful environment offer an unforgettable experience for nature lovers and underwater explorers.

Bai Nho – Ganh Hang

Located about 10 kilometers from the island center, Bai Nho – Ganh Hang features a crescent-shaped beach framed by rocky cliffs. Despite its small size, the beach is airy, quiet, and blessed with clear turquoise water.

Visitors can swim, snorkel, relax on the grass-covered cliffs, or simply sit on the rocks and admire the endless sky. Afterward, enjoying fresh and affordable seafood such as herring salad, grilled sea urchin, braised squid, or cobia sour soup is a must.

Hon Tranh Beach

Hon Tranh Beach is famous for its calm waters, exceptional visibility, and vibrant coral reefs. Surrounded by volcanic rocks and protected by high cliffs, the sea remains tranquil year-round. The blend of blue sea, clear sky, and rugged black rocks creates a dramatic natural masterpiece.

Swimming, snorkeling, and watching the sunset here offer a deeply immersive experience, making Hon Tranh Beach one of the most memorable stops on any Phu Quy Island journey.

With its majestic scenery, pristine beaches, and rich cultural heritage, Phu Quy Island promises unforgettable discoveries for travelers visiting Binh Thuan. If you are planning a weekend getaway or a longer island escape, these remarkable attractions should not be missed.
